getObjectsV1.description: DISCOVERY: Start unknown-asset searches here. MCP defaults to root=true and limit=50 (maximum 500); follow pagination.nextOffset with the same filters until there is no next page when the requested mapped-model scope must be enumerated. Results contain i3X ElementIds and display names and describe the i3X-mapped model, not necessarily every node on the upstream OPC UA server. Do not call these OPC UA NodeIds; use resolveElementIdsToNodeIds for source NodeIds and getBrowsePath for a mapped browse path. Set root=false only when the user explicitly requests full mapped-model enumeration. Navigate from returned ElementIds with queryRelatedObjectsV1. Never guess typeElementId values such as "plc"; filter only with an exact known type ID. State the enumerated scope and disclose truncation or unavailable coverage; never claim the remote address space is complete from this listing.

queryRelatedObjectsV1.description: NAVIGATION: Follow hierarchy, composition, and graph relationships from one or a few discovered i3X ElementIds. MCP defaults to 50 related objects per source (maximum 500); use body.offset with the same elementIds until there is no nextOffset. Results are mapped objects, not OPC UA NodeIds; use resolveElementIdsToNodeIds for source IDs. Follow only the relevant branch to connected equipment, components, properties, Memory, or DataBlocks. Leave relationshipType unset unless its exact value is known. This navigates the i3X-mapped model, not the full upstream OPC UA address space; report the scope actually traversed.

queryLastKnownValuesV1.description: READ CURRENT VALUES only after discovering the target property's exact i3X ElementId; do not pass an OPC UA NodeId here. Batch only a few relevant property IDs and use maxDepth=1. Do not read container objects that have no value. To read many properties under one known container without generating a long ID array, use readContainerValues. History is a separate tool. Preserve value, quality, and source timestamp; a last-known value may be stale.

readContainerValues.description: READ MANY CURRENT VALUES under one discovered container in one short tool call. Pass the exact containerId from discovery/navigation; the server finds descendant properties and reads up to 50 per page (50 maximum). When nextOffset is returned, pass it as offset to continue. Do not use on a plant root or broad asset unless the user requests all its values. Returns each property's name, ID, value, quality, and timestamp; it does not read container values or history.

queryHistoricalValuesV1.description: READ HISTORY only when the user asks for past values or a trend. Supply discovered i3X ElementIds (not OPC UA NodeIds) and a narrow startTime/endTime interval; use maxDepth=1 unless component history is needed. MCP defaults to 100 samples per page (maximum 500). Continue with body.offset using each successful result's result.pagination.nextOffset until that result has no nextOffset. A successful model lookup or history-capability declaration does not prove that a variable has stored history; inspect per-item failures. For current state use queryLastKnownValuesV1.

listObjectsByIdV1.description: Fetch specific objects by exact i3X ElementIds already returned by discovery or navigation. Keep the ID list narrow. This is a lookup, not discovery; start unknown asset searches with getObjectsV1(root=true). Use getElementContext and resolveElementIdsToNodeIds when model context and source NodeId evidence are needed. A missing mapped result does not prove the node is absent from the remote OPC UA address space.

getInfoV1.description: GATEWAY INFO: Return metadata about this i3X API gateway, including its i3X version and capabilities. This is not the connected OPC UA server's product name, software version, or ServerStatus. For upstream server status use getUaStatus; for this gateway's connection state and configured endpoint use getUaConnection. For model-reported server identity, inspect a mapped OPC UA Server object instance whose type is the standard ServerType (ns=0;i=2004), then inspect its ServerStatus property. If it is absent from the mapped model, do not infer that the upstream server lacks it; use getUaStatus for a direct ServerStatus read.

getModelMetricsV1.description: Return aggregate counts and build/topology metrics for the current i3X-mapped model snapshot. Use for mapped-model size questions instead of listing objects just to count them. These are not remote-server totals and do not establish complete address-space coverage or capabilities. Label counts as mapped-model counts.

getModelNamespaceGapsV1.description: Report gaps in mapping OPC UA namespace metadata into the current i3X model. Use only for mapping diagnostics. This does not discover assets or establish that unmapped remote nodes are absent.

getNamespacesV1.description: ADVANCED: List OPC UA namespace URIs reported by the connected upstream server, only when asked about namespaces or diagnosing a mapping issue. Namespace presence does not prove companion-specification conformance, node coverage, or support for every feature in that namespace. Do not start asset discovery here; use getObjectsV1(root=true). Namespace output may be lengthy.

getObjectTypesV1.description: ADVANCED SCHEMA LOOKUP: Use only for explicit type/schema questions, not asset discovery. MCP defaults to compact type summaries in pages of 50 (maximum 500); use pagination.nextOffset to continue and queryObjectTypesV1 for a selected schema. The catalog may include synthesized model types and is not a feature-support checklist. Find assets first with getObjectsV1(root=true), then navigate.

queryObjectTypesV1.description: Look up type schemas for exact discovered type elementIds when type details are required. Prefer a narrow lookup over getObjectTypesV1, which lists the mapped type catalog. A type definition or namespace is not proof that all instances/features are present or conformant. Not for asset discovery or reading values.

getRelationshipTypesV1.description: ADVANCED: Use only when the user asks for relationship vocabulary or a relationship name is needed but unavailable from navigation results. MCP defaults to compact entries in pages of 50 (maximum 500); continue with pagination.nextOffset. This returns i3X relationships and mapped graph relationship types, not every OPC UA ReferenceType. Do not call before asset discovery.

queryRelationshipTypesV1.description: Look up relationship types for exact elementIds when relationship schema details are explicitly needed. Prefer this narrow lookup over getRelationshipTypesV1. Not a substitute for navigating actual relationships with queryRelatedObjectsV1.

getUaStatus.description: UPSTREAM OPC UA SERVER: Directly read the standard ServerStatus variable from the connected remote endpoint (NodeId i=2256; Objects/Server/ServerStatus). This is remote-server status, not i3X gateway health. Prefer this when ServerStatus is requested but the mapped Server object/property is absent. Report returned fields as-is; a failed read does not prove the standard node is unsupported.

getUaConnection.description: GATEWAY CONNECTION: Return this i3X gateway's OPC UA client connection snapshot: state, configured remote endpoint URI, and time in that state. This describes the gateway-to-server link; it does not identify the remote server's product/version, uptime, or supported features. If only connectivity is known and ServerStatus could not be read, report this as connection evidence, not remote-server identity.

getUaLimits.description: UPSTREAM CONNECTION LIMITS: Return the operational limits and subscription capability values reported by the connected OPC UA server through this gateway. Use for questions about these specific limits. Null or absent limits are unknown; listed limits do not establish full OPC UA specification conformance or unrelated feature support.

getUaMetrics.description: GATEWAY CLIENT METRICS: Return OPC UA request counters observed by this i3X gateway client, including reads, writes, browses, history operations, and failures. These are gateway-observed counters, not server-wide diagnostics or proof that the remote server supports every counted operation.

createSubscriptionV1.description: STATE-CHANGING: Create an ongoing value-monitoring subscription only when explicitly requested. First discover the exact property i3X ElementIds and select only relevant signals; do not use for one-time reads or infer that a subscription proves general server PubSub support. This creates gateway-managed monitoring state.

registerMonitoredItemsV1.description: STATE-CHANGING: Add exact, previously discovered property i3X ElementIds to an existing gateway-managed subscription when explicitly requested. Do not pass OPC UA NodeIds, containers, or guessed IDs. This changes which values the subscription monitors; use queryLastKnownValuesV1 for a one-time read.

removeMonitoredItemsV1.description: STATE-CHANGING: Remove specified monitored items from an existing subscription only when explicitly requested. Use the exact subscription and monitored-item identifiers from context; this stops those monitored updates and does not read values.

syncSubscriptionV1.description: FETCH AND ACKNOWLEDGE: Retrieve pending updates for the identified gateway-managed subscription. Acknowledge only after the updates have been successfully retrieved and processed; do not acknowledge updates you have not incorporated into the answer/workflow. This is not a one-time current-value read; use queryLastKnownValuesV1 for that.

deleteSubscriptionsV1.description: DESTRUCTIVE STATE CHANGE: Delete only the exact gateway-managed subscription IDs the user explicitly asked to stop/remove. Verify the target IDs from context first; deletion stops that subscription's monitoring. This does not delete an OPC UA server-side subscription outside this gateway's management.

listSubscriptionsV1.description: List gateway-managed subscriptions to inspect their configuration/status when asked. This is not a complete inventory of every subscription or monitored item on the remote OPC UA server, and it does not discover assets or read current model values.

industrial_discovery_workflow.description: Find assets and answers using the smallest safe discovery path
industrial_discovery_workflow.template:
Answer this industrial-model question: {{question}}

Keep evidence sources distinct: getInfoV1 describes this i3X gateway; getUaStatus reads ServerStatus from the upstream OPC UA endpoint; getUaConnection describes the gateway's connection to that endpoint; model tools describe only the mapped model. Never infer remote product/version/features from gateway metadata, mapped-model counts, namespace names, or request counters.

Before drafting, maintain a compact evidence ledger: claim; exact tool result; scope; i3X ElementId; OPC UA source NodeId and mapped path if returned; evidence class (direct read, mapped-model presence, declared capability, or unknown). Do not cite an ID/path unless it was returned or resolved. Never label an i3X ElementId as an OPC UA NodeId.

Choose tools by purpose: getObjectsV1(root=true) for unknown top-level assets; queryRelatedObjectsV1 to navigate known IDs; findElementsByName for display-name substrings; searchModelElements for focused metadata/type/role/namespace/relationship searches; getElementContext for one known element; getChildren for direct children on a selected plane; getCompositionProperties for recursive composition properties without values. Use getBrowsePath for mapped display paths and resolveElementIdsToNodeIds for source NodeIds. Do not make unfiltered searches expecting exhaustive results.

For values, first discover exact i3X property ElementIds. Use queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1) for a few current values, readContainerValues for many descendant values under one known focused container, and queryHistoricalValuesV1 only for requested history. Check each item's success/error; preserve value, quality, timestamp, and state that last-known values may be stale. A history declaration does not prove stored history for a particular variable; a model action/alarm/property does not prove it is operational or safe to use.

If the user asks for "all", paginate to completion within each relevant tool's scope and report the scope, page completion, failures, and truncation. Clearly say "all items returned in the i3X-mapped model" when that is the scope; do not claim complete remote address-space coverage unless directly established. A namespace or type does not prove companion-specification conformance. Do not infer implementation library/version, writable control behavior, active alarms, or MES readiness without direct evidence.

Finish every requested section or label it incomplete and explain why. Separate observations from recommendations; make recommendations conditional on evidence. Do not fill gaps with assumptions or silently convert failed lookups into absence.

opcua_endpoint_analysis.description: Analyze the connected upstream OPC UA endpoint using its MCP evidence guide and Audit Mode; distinguish endpoint facts from Gateway and mapped-model evidence
opcua_endpoint_analysis.template:
Answer this upstream OPC UA endpoint question: {{question}}

Use listMcpResources and readMcpResource to read i3x://guides/opcua-analysis before analysis. For mapping or mapped-model claims, also read i3x://guides/opcua-i3x-mapping and/or i3x://guides/i3x-model-analysis. Follow the guide's OPC UA Audit Mode for this endpoint assessment.

Use an evidence ledger for each factual claim: tool and exact returned field; label (observed, inferred, verified, or unknown); scope/time; evidence class (direct read, mapped-model presence, declared capability, or unknown); i3X ElementId; OPC UA instance ExpandedNodeId; OPC UA TypeDefinition ExpandedNodeId; path only if returned or resolved. Never substitute an ElementId or type NodeId for the instance NodeId. Prefer returned ExpandedNodeIds; never invent IDs or guess namespace indexes.

Keep sources separate: getInfoV1 is i3X gateway metadata; getUaStatus directly reads upstream ServerStatus (NodeId i=2256); getUaConnection is the gateway-to-endpoint connection state/URI; model searches, namespaces, types, and metrics cover only what is mapped or observed. None alone proves complete remote address-space visibility or overall feature support.

For Server identity, search the mapped model for a candidate Server object; inspect it with getElementContext and verify standard ServerType (NodeId i=2004) from returned source-type metadata. A name match is insufficient. Resolve source NodeIds with resolveElementIdsToNodeIds. If the verified mapped ServerStatus property exists and its value is requested, read its exact discovered i3X ElementId. If it is absent or unmapped, call getUaStatus; a failed call is not proof the standard node is unsupported. Use getUaConnection only as narrower evidence if the question is connectivity, never as remote identity evidence.

For "all" requests, follow nextOffset until it is absent or report the inventory as partial with query scope, count, filters, failures, and nextOffset. Completed pagination covers only that query and mapped-model scope, not necessarily the remote address space. Namespace URI observed does not mean Companion Specification implemented, conformant, or certified. History declarations do not prove HistoryRead success or returned samples. Method existence or Executable=true does not establish caller authorization, successful invocation, or operational effect. Do not infer implementation version, active alarms, per-variable history availability, writable control behavior, or MES readiness without direct evidence. State failed, missing, truncated, and unknown results explicitly. Include missing evidence and do not recommend enabling unverified capabilities. Finish requested sections or identify any incomplete section and why.

inspect_asset.description: Inspect one named asset and report its relevant structure or requested properties
inspect_asset.template:
Inspect asset {{asset_name}} for this request: {{question}}

Start with getObjectsV1(root=true) only if the asset elementId is not already known. Match the returned asset by name; never guess IDs or typeElementId values. Navigate from that asset with queryRelatedObjectsV1 and follow only the branch needed to answer. For a current value, locate the named property first, then call queryLastKnownValuesV1 on only its exact elementId with maxDepth=1. Do not read container values or history unless explicitly requested. Avoid global object/type/namespace listings. Return concise findings with source object/property names.

inspect_signal.description: Locate one named signal and return its current value or requested details
inspect_signal.template:
Find signal {{signal_name}} under asset {{asset_name}}.

If the asset ID is unknown, call getObjectsV1(root=true), match the asset by name, then navigate relevant relationships with queryRelatedObjectsV1. Continue from returned IDs until the named property is found. Do not guess IDs, use guessed typeElementId filters, or list the whole model. Read only the matching property's current value with queryLastKnownValuesV1(elementIds=[exact property ID], maxDepth=1). Do not query history unless requested. Report value, quality, timestamp, and the matched property path; if no match exists, say so.

inspect_plc.description: Find a connected PLC and inspect requested PLC data such as OrderNumber, firmware, DataBlocks, or Memory variables
inspect_plc.template:
For asset {{asset_name}}, answer: {{question}}

If needed, discover top-level assets with getObjectsV1(root=true); identify the named asset from returned data. Use queryRelatedObjectsV1 with actual returned elementIds to find the connected PLC/controller, then navigate only the PLC branch. Never guess IDs or typeElementId values such as "plc". For OrderNumber or firmware version, locate the exact property and read it with queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1). For DataBlock counts or Memory variables, navigate to the relevant collection/container and count/list the returned entries; do not read container values. If asked for many current values under one container, use readContainerValues with the exact containerId instead of assembling property IDs. Avoid full-model scans and type/namespace catalogs. State what was found and distinguish absent data from an unsuccessful lookup.

machine_health_snapshot.description: Summarize current machine condition using relevant signals and only requested history
machine_health_snapshot.template:
Assess machine {{asset_id}}. Lookback: {{lookback_minutes}} minutes.

If asset_id is a name rather than an elementId, discover roots with getObjectsV1(root=true) and match it. Navigate only relevant components/signals with queryRelatedObjectsV1. Read current values only for relevant properties using queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1). Query historical values only for those signals and only within the stated lookback if trend evidence is needed. Do not enumerate the model or inspect type/namespace catalogs. Summarize evidence, uncertainty, severity, and safe checks; do not infer unsupported failure causes.

alarm_triage.description: Triage an alarm using narrow asset navigation and relevant signal evidence
alarm_triage.template:
Triage alarm {{alarm_text}} for asset {{asset_id}}. Relevant window: {{time_window}}.

If the asset ID is unknown, call getObjectsV1(root=true) and match by name. Navigate only related alarm/process signals using queryRelatedObjectsV1. Read current values for relevant properties with queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1); use queryHistoricalValuesV1 only for those known signal IDs and the specified window. Do not scan all objects or types. Separate observed facts from hypotheses and provide safe, non-invasive operator checks; do not recommend bypassing safeguards.

predictive_maintenance_check.description: Assess degradation using selected signals and bounded history
predictive_maintenance_check.template:
Assess degradation risk for asset {{asset_id}} over {{lookback_days}} days.

Resolve an unknown asset using getObjectsV1(root=true), then queryRelatedObjectsV1 only for relevant condition signals. Read current values for selected properties with queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1). Use queryHistoricalValuesV1 for only those signal IDs and the stated period. Do not enumerate the full model. State evidence and uncertainty, recommend inspections, and suggest subscriptions only if ongoing monitoring is requested.

process_drift_analysis.description: Analyze a named KPI for drift using only relevant assets and signals
process_drift_analysis.template:
Analyze {{kpi_name}} for {{line_or_cell}} over {{lookback_hours}} hours.

If the line/cell is not identified by elementId, discover roots with getObjectsV1(root=true), then navigate the matching asset using queryRelatedObjectsV1. Find only the KPI and directly relevant signals. Query history for those known IDs and the requested time window; read current values only if needed. Do not list the whole model or object types. Report observed drift, evidence, and plausible causes separately; do not recommend unverified control-limit changes.

downtime_root_cause.description: Reconstruct a downtime event from selected signals in the stated interval
downtime_root_cause.template:
Analyze downtime for {{asset_id}} from {{downtime_start}} to {{downtime_end}}.

Resolve the asset with getObjectsV1(root=true) only if its ID is unknown, then navigate only relevant components and signals with queryRelatedObjectsV1. Query historical values for selected signal IDs over the event interval; use maxDepth=1 unless component history is necessary. Read current values only for post-event status. Avoid full-model scans. Distinguish confirmed telemetry from inferred causes and summarize timeline, containment, and follow-up.

energy_intensity_review.description: Review energy patterns for a named asset or line using selected measurements
energy_intensity_review.template:
Review energy use for {{asset_or_line}} over {{lookback_days}} days. Production context: {{production_context}}.

If needed, discover the asset with getObjectsV1(root=true), then navigate only relevant energy and production signals using queryRelatedObjectsV1. Query history only for those property IDs and the stated period; use current values only if needed for operating state. Do not enumerate the full model or type catalog. Separate measured patterns from estimates and list concise, evidence-based opportunities.

opcua_data_quality_audit.description: Check telemetry quality for selected signals without scanning the full model
opcua_data_quality_audit.template:
Audit data quality for asset {{asset_id}} over {{lookback_hours}} hours.

Resolve an unknown asset with getObjectsV1(root=true), then use queryRelatedObjectsV1 to select only relevant properties. Use queryLastKnownValuesV1 for freshness and queryHistoricalValuesV1 for continuity only on those IDs and within the stated period. Do not call getObjectsV1 without root=true, and do not inspect namespaces unless a mapping issue is explicitly suspected. Report observed missingness, staleness, timestamp/value anomalies, and limits of the evidence.

shift_handover_summary.description: Create a concise handover from relevant current state and the stated shift interval
shift_handover_summary.template:
Prepare a handover for {{area}} covering {{shift_window}}.

If the area is not identified, discover roots with getObjectsV1(root=true), then navigate only relevant assets/signals using queryRelatedObjectsV1. Read current values for selected properties with queryLastKnownValuesV1(maxDepth=1). Use history only for relevant signals in the shift window. Inspect subscriptions only if pending monitored updates are specifically relevant. Avoid full-model enumeration. Summarize events, unresolved issues, evidence, and next-shift checks.

i3x_context_mapping_assistant.description: Review existing i3X context for a mapping task using the OPC UA-to-i3X mapping guide and evidence boundaries; use schema catalogs only when requested
i3x_context_mapping_assistant.template:
Review {{asset_id_or_namespace}} for this mapping goal: {{mapping_goal}}.

Use listMcpResources and readMcpResource to read i3x://guides/opcua-i3x-mapping. For mapped-model evidence, also read i3x://guides/i3x-model-analysis; for upstream endpoint claims, read i3x://guides/opcua-analysis. Keep OPC UA instance ExpandedNodeIds, TypeDefinition ExpandedNodeIds, and i3X ElementIds separate; prefer returned ExpandedNodeIds and never invent IDs. A namespace URI, profile match, type association, or capability declaration does not prove implementation, conformance, certification, or runtime operation.

For an asset, start with getObjectsV1(root=true) if needed and navigate the relevant branch with queryRelatedObjectsV1. Do not enumerate all objects. Use getNamespacesV1 only when namespace alignment is part of the task. Use getObjectTypesV1 or getRelationshipTypesV1 only when the mapping goal requires vocabulary/schema details; prefer targeted query tools when exact IDs are known. If nextOffset is present, continue pagination or report the result as partial; completed pagination is limited to the exact query and mapped-model scope. Report only relevant observed objects, links, gaps, evidence, and a minimal mapping checklist. Distinguish observed facts, inferences, verified behavior, and unknowns.
